finding: A specific, edition-bearing bibliographic candidate was identified for the Tabari text family: Jami al-bayan, edited by Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muhsin al-Turki with Dar Hajr / its Islamic Research and Studies Center, first edition 1422 AH / 2001 CE. The Shamela catalog explicitly records the edition, editor, publisher, place, date, volume structure, and says its electronic text was newly entered based on al-Turki's edition. Its Juz Amma section is volume 24 and its pagination is marked as matching the printed edition. Waqfeya independently catalogs the al-Turki/Dar Hajr work and exposes a scan entry for volume 24 (Juz Amma). This establishes a strong candidate edition to compare. It does NOT establish that KSU's text or live source ID 310 came from this exact edition: the accessible Shamela pages inspected in this run did not yet reach the 108:3 passage and its notes 7-9 for direct collation against the KSU witness. Waqfeya and Shamela also describe volume counts differently (25 listed volumes versus 26 parts including indexes), so packaging/counting was not normalized.

source_anchors.evidence: Names al-Tabari, editor Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muhsin al-Turki, publication 1422/2001, Dar Hajr, and lists volume 24 as Juz Amma; download list includes volume 24 scan entry.
source_anchors.limitations: Catalog-level evidence only; linked scan was inaccessible to the browser reader during this run; not a direct 108:3 collation.

source_anchors.evidence: Identifies al-Turki's investigation with Dar Hajr's Research and Islamic Studies Center, Dar Hajr, Cairo, first edition 1422/2001, 26 parts (24 text volumes plus indexes), and states this electronic text was newly entered based on the al-Turki edition with printed pagination.
source_anchors.limitations: This supports edition identification for the Shamela text, not provenance of the KSU/Mosshaf source or numeric source ID 310.
